name: Hadassah
overview: Hadassah was a female figure known primarily as the cousin of Mordecai, as stated in Esther 2:7. Her tribal affiliation and additional personal notes are not recorded in Scripture. Her identity is closely connected to her familial relationship with Mordecai.
namesAndTitles: Hadassah means 'myrtle' and possibly 'bride,' reflecting a Hebrew origin, while her Persian name Esther means 'star,' possibly linked to the goddess Ishtar. She is also known by the title 'Queen Esther,' indicating her royal status as recorded in Esther 2:7 and 2:22.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hadassah as the cousin and daughter of Mordecai, as well as the daughter of Abihail (Esther 2:7, 2:15). These relationships establish her within a known family lineage important to the biblical narrative.
scriptureSignificance: Hadassah's significance arises from her role as Esther, who became queen and was positioned to influence the Persian court. Her connection to Mordecai situates her within God's providential plan for the Jewish people during exile, highlighting her as a key instrument in preserving Israel.
